verdict.rationale: Proa documents explicit, typed data passing: compile-time-checked props, signals plus event handlers for interactive islands, and typed access to request and route state through WebContext. Together these suggest explicit data flow, but the evidence never states a one-way data-flow model, never rules out two-way bindings, and shows no state-change tracing or debugging tools. Missing for 10: an explicit unidirectional data-flow or no-two-way-binding guarantee, documentation of how signal state changes propagate and can be traced, debugging or devtools for state changes, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trace state changes through explicit, predictable data flow instead of debugging implicit two-way bindings

citations.quote: the fields passed to AboutPage are compile-time-checked props.
Add signals and event handlers, and Proa emits the server-rendered HTML plus the JavaScript required for that island
